onboarding.welcome_title: Find out what’s behind your bad gut days.
onboarding.welcome_1: Log meals, stool and how you feel in under a minute a day.
onboarding.welcome_2: Over months, it looks for foods that tend to come before bad days — and says how sure it is.
onboarding.welcome_3: Then it helps you test a suspicion properly, with a short structured trial.
onboarding.disclaimer_body: FoodTrack is a wellness tool, not a medical device. It never diagnoses anything. If it notices a warning sign, it will tell you to see a doctor.
onboarding.goal_title: What are you trying to figure out?
onboarding.goal_body: Track what I eat and my weight
onboarding.trackers_title: Which of these do you want to track?

why.checkin: Sleep and stress make the food findings much more trustworthy.
why.weight: Trend line, and a safety check.
why.medication: Painkillers and antibiotics change the gut — the analysis needs to know.
why.event_marker: Travel, illness, antibiotics — big shocks to the gut.

how.title: How this works
how.p1: You log what you ate, your bowel movements, any symptoms, and a short evening check-in. Nothing is mandatory; a bare time is still useful.
how.p2: After about three weeks, the app starts comparing days: how often did a bad gut day follow a food, compared with days without it — 6 to 72 hours later.
how.p3: Every finding shows its evidence: how many days, how big the difference, how sure, and what else might explain it.
how.p4: A finding is an association, not proof. To test a suspicion, the app can set up a short trial: remove the food, then bring it back in steps.
how.p5: This is a slow tool. A clear effect usually takes 3–4 months of logging to show; a subtle one 6 months or more.
how.p6: Your data stays on your own server. Meal text may be sent to the language model you configured to understand it; stool, symptoms, mood and weight never are.

trial.no_live_estimate: I’ll show the result at the end. Knowing early changes how you rate things.

design_explain.A: Remove it completely for a while, then bring it back in steps and see what happens.
design_explain.B: You eat this most days, so: four days with, four days without, in turns.
design_explain.C: Your usual amount, then half, then a quarter — no full removal.
design_explain.D: You won’t know which days get the real thing and which get an inert control. It’s the only honest way to separate the food from expecting it.

trial.blind_option: Make it blinded ({dose} vs an inert control)
trial.baseline_reused: Your last two weeks are well logged, so they serve as the baseline.
trial.why_three_weeks: Three weeks is the shortest window that can actually answer this. A two-week version would probably come back “inconclusive”, which wastes the effort of doing it.
trial.prereg_line: It counts as a trigger only if the difference is at least {mie}.
trial.locked_note: Fixed before the data is seen, so the answer can’t move. A reintroduction is always part of it.
trial.power_ok: This design is long enough to answer the question.
trial.power_low: This design is probably too short to answer the question — a longer elimination would help.
trial.power_unknown: I couldn’t check the length right now.

trial.adherence_so_far: Followed the plan on {pct}% of days so far.
trial.guess_question: Which do you think you got in the last period?
trial.guess_why: There’s no right answer — it measures how much expectation is part of this.
trial.record_slip: Record a slip on that day
trial.slip_extend: Record it and extend the trial by 2 days
trial.stop_early: Stop early and see what it shows
trial.stop_confirm: Stop now? You’ll get a verdict on what’s been collected, labelled as partial.
trial.abandon_why: What happened? This only improves future suggestions.
trial.prep_1: Fill identical opaque containers: half with the real powder, half with the control.
trial.prep_2: Ask someone else to label each envelope below at random, keeping the key — or use the app’s sealed allocation and let a friend pack them.
trial.prep_3: Take the envelope for each period on its dates. You’ll be asked what you think you got.
trial.exposure_prompt: A meal may have had {name} in it ({items}). Count it as a slip?

reminders.privacy: Notifications never mention a symptom, a food or a finding. Warning signs are never sent as notifications — they wait in the app.

security.protects: Your meal text, notes, photos and food names are encrypted on the server. A stolen database copy doesn’t reveal “went to my brother’s, ate too much at the barbecue”, or a photo of your kitchen.
security.leaks: It still shows the shape of things: that you logged a type-7 stool on the 14th, a bloating score that evening, your weight trend. The numbers stay readable because the analysis needs them.
security.card_explain: Keep a printed copy off the server and away from your backups. Showing it needs your passphrase and is logged.
security.rate_limited: Too many requests — try again in an hour.
security.card_invalid: This card doesn’t match. Print a fresh one.
security.rotation_cli: Rotating keys is done on the server only (pnpm keys:rotate-kek), never from the app.
